intro: When you search for an agriculture solicitor near me, you likely need legal help with the land, tenancy or business side of farming. Agricultural solicitors deal with the special rules that apply to farmland, and finding one who understands your situation locally can make a real difference. We introduce you to a suitable UK professional who will quote you directly, with fees on application.
need_heading: What people searching for an agriculture solicitor near me usually need
need_lead: The situations that lead to this search are often practical and time-sensitive, and they usually involve land, family or money.
needs: You are taking on or giving up a farm tenancy and need to understand the special legislation that applies to agricultural tenancies.
You are planning how to pass the farm on to the next generation and want advice on succession so the farm stays viable.
You are buying or selling farmland and need help with the legal side, including rights of way and any environmental schemes attached to the land.
You are setting up or dissolving a farming partnership and need the agreement to reflect how the farm actually works.
You want to understand agricultural property relief and how it might affect the future of the farm business.
context_heading: One key thing to understand about agricultural solicitors
context: Agricultural tenancies and farmland have their own body of law, so it helps to speak to a solicitor who regularly advises farmers and landowners rather than one who mainly deals with residential property. In England and Wales, solicitors are regulated by the Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA), and you can check an individual or firm on the SRA's register. In Scotland the regulator is the Law Society of Scotland, and in Northern Ireland it is the Law Society of Northern Ireland.

Regulated firms must hold professional indemnity insurance and have a complaints procedure. If a service complaint is not resolved, the Legal Ombudsman can look at it in England and Wales. The word "lawyer" is not protected on its own, so check that whoever handles your matter is a solicitor, a chartered legal executive (CILEx) or another authorised professional. Reserved activities such as conducting court litigation and certain probate and conveyancing work can only be carried out by authorised people.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Say where the farm or land is, as agricultural law differs across the UK and a local solicitor may be more familiar with the relevant rules.
Describe the type of matter, such as a tenancy, land sale, succession planning, partnership or rights of way issue.
Mention any deadlines you are working towards, such as a date for exchanging contracts or a tenancy start date.
Explain whether the land is owned or tenanted, and whether any environmental schemes are involved.
Include the size of the farm or landholding in general terms, as this can affect the complexity of the work.
Note if other family members or business partners are involved, so the solicitor knows who they may need to speak to.
questions: How much experience do you have with agricultural tenancies and the special legislation that applies to them?
What would you need from me to advise on succession planning for the farm?
Can you explain how agricultural property relief might apply to our situation?
Will you handle the matter yourself or pass it to a colleague, and are they authorised to do this work?
What are your fees and how will you keep me informed as the work progresses?
How do you approach rights of way and environmental scheme issues on farmland?

faqs.q: Do I need a solicitor who specialises in agriculture rather than a general practice?
faqs.a: Agricultural tenancies have special legislation, and farmland sales often involve rights of way and environmental schemes. A solicitor who regularly advises farmers and landowners will be more familiar with these areas, so it is worth asking about their experience before you instruct them.

faqs.q: Can iComply recommend a specific agriculture solicitor near me?
faqs.a: We introduce you to a suitable UK professional based on what you tell us, but we do not recommend or endorse any particular solicitor. You decide whether to instruct them after speaking with them and checking their details on the relevant regulator's register.

faqs.q: How do I check that a solicitor is properly regulated?
faqs.a: In England and Wales, check the Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA) register. In Scotland, check with the Law Society of Scotland, and in Northern Ireland with the Law Society of Northern Ireland. This confirms whether the individual or firm is regulated and authorised to carry out reserved legal work.

faqs.q: What information should I have ready before I speak to a solicitor about a farm tenancy?
faqs.a: It helps to have the tenancy agreement, any correspondence about the tenancy, and details of the land involved. If the matter concerns succession or a partnership, bring any existing wills, partnership agreements or family trust documents you have.
